evidence.claim: The hole statistics reproduce: 7.3% of GT nodes have no final node within 4 um, and hole-touching edges carry 62% of FN edge-ends. 54% of hole RUNS last 1 frame (hypothesis: 51.5%). Weighted by nodes, though, only 23% of hole nodes are in 1-frame runs, 36% in runs of 2 frames or less, and 27% in runs of 2 frames or less that have covered GT nodes on both sides (24% on 44b6, 28% on 6bba). Most hole nodes are persistent runs, not flicker.
evidence.source: LOCAL measurement, 40 videos (first 20 6bba plus every 5th 44b6 up to 20), 21,453 GT nodes, exp39+ef final graph (tail divnet_rerank_fb435c47e6d4 + official match cache __ef_7500fcb4b5); script scratchpad/holes.py

evidence.claim: The temporal sandwich does not discriminate. With q = the GT position, 44% of holes pass (a kept node at both t-1 and t+1 within 6 um). Random in-tissue control points (4.5-7 um from a kept node, clearance >4.5 um) pass 40%. Only a 4 um sandwich separates them (3.6% vs 0.6%), and it reaches almost no holes.

IMAGE TEST: most holes are NOT a missing nucleus. The test takes the brightest smoothed-intensity point within 2 um of the hole GT node and draws a line to the nearest final node. Holes at 4-5 um show a dip (valley <0.85) in 1.2% of cases (<0.95: 4.7%, n=169); holes at 5-6 um in 0% (<0.95: 5.3%, n=132). Two DISTINCT detected neighbour nuclei 4.5-8 um apart dip in 46% of cases (median 0.86, q10 0.62). Close-matched GT nodes give 1.0 at every quantile. Holes at 6-7 um dip in 11% (<0.95: 30%); holes beyond 7 um dip in 44% (<0.95: 59%), like distinct nuclei. The picture is the same in both embryos (44b6 at 4-6 um: 0% <0.85). So the ~73% of hole nodes at 4-6 um sit on the SAME imaged blob as our nearest node: the GT and our node sit on opposite sides of one nucleus. That is an annotation or localisation offset, not a missing detection, and a node added there would be a duplicate.
evidence.source: LOCAL, 12 videos (6 per embryo), raw train zarr, gaussian sigma z/y/x = 0.6/1.5/1.5 voxels (scratchpad/holes_img.py)

evidence.claim: FN edge-ends by distance to the nearest node: 4-5 um 8.8%, 5-6 um 12.3%, 6-7 um 9.6%, >7 um 31.8% (FN rate 100%, = the a_never/tail/linefit classes). Holes beyond 7 um pass the 6 um sandwich only 1.5% of the time: they are persistent misses (77% 'side_far'), so the sandwich cannot reach the genuinely missing nuclei either.

Only 12% of hole GT nodes have a checkpoint (post-ILP/gap, pre-tail) real node within 3 um (24% within 4 um). A minority of holes are therefore created by tail, linefit or edge-filter pruning rather than by the detector.
evidence.source: LOCAL, 40 videos, friend A ckpt npz tzyx_syn

evidence.claim: The forum already reports annotation offsets. Kaggle annotations sit on Ultrack-segmentation points, which are sometimes 'cell corners' rather than centres, and duplicate nodes near an annotated cell steal its links (hengck23). A blind human review found ~70% of one team's FPs could be TPs (sghwr). A constant offset correction loses 0.0031, and only a learned per-node offset pays (Le Quang Canh). This matches the same-blob finding.

x138's parent (thtennant frontier947-readmit-v1, 0.946) already has a sub-threshold node path: readmit (ILP-discarded peaks >=0.965, more than 2 um from any node and within 4 um of an open end/start, then relink again) and gapfill (end t -> start t+g+1, g<=3, only through free peaks >=0.5 within 3.5 um of the straight line, exclude radius 2 um, <=3% added nodes, from a low-detection dump >=0.3). Both were neutral on LB against our line.

The literature fixes missed detections with an over-complete candidate set plus global selection, not local fill rules. linajea extracts NMS maxima above a low per-dataset threshold, and its ILP node cost wV*(s_i - tauV) lets it select weak candidates when they are temporally consistent. Ultrack solves an ILP over multi-hypothesis segments. ByteTrack's second association matches low-score boxes ONLY to still-unmatched tracklets (= our readmit). None of them inserts a candidate beside an already-matched track.
evidence.source: Malin-Mayor et al., linajea, bioRxiv 10.1101/2021.07.28.454016 (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2021.07.28.454016v1.full); Ultrack, Nat Methods 2025 (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-025-02778-0); ByteTrack arXiv 2110.06864 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06864)

evidence.claim: Friend A's full-frame 0.90 pass yields +24% candidate peaks at least 3 um from existing nodes (up to 73% in one video). Clearance 4.5 um plus the 6 um sandwich (40% pass in-tissue) would keep far more than 1.5%, so the rank cap would decide what gets in, not the rule.

implementation_notes: WHY IT FAILS: (1) The hole majority (nearest node 4-6 um, ~73% of hole nodes, ~21% of FN edge-ends) is one nucleus seen from two sides: our node on one flank, the GT annotation on the other (no intensity valley in ~95-99% of cases, vs a dip in about half of distinct neighbour pairs). A 0.90 peak near such a GT node is a second mode of the SAME nucleus. Adding it produces exactly the duplicate that steals links (forum), and because the detector was trained on these annotations, such flank peaks are in-sample on train: optimistic locally, costly on test. Clearance 4.5 um does not prevent this, because these holes are by definition 4-6 um from the kept node. (2) The sandwich (kept nodes within 6 um at t-1 and t+1) fires for 40% of random in-tissue points, so it adds no selectivity. (3) The genuinely missing nuclei (>7 um holes, ~32% of FN edge-ends, = the a_never class) are persistent runs with nothing kept nearby, so the sandwich reaches 1.5% of them. The x138 gapfill and B35 step A already work that territory. PITFALLS FOUND: the tail edge list is pre-edge-filter (the edge filter prunes a few nodes, so filter by the match n_id); coords_exp39.parquet holds only division-triple nodes, not the full graph; the raw geff is the ILP solution only (no discarded >=0.965 peaks), so step 0 needs friend A's peaks90 cache or the x138 lowdet dump. Any new short track also has to survive min_track_len 6 unless it attaches to an existing track. SPIN-OFF (GT-free and cheap, worth handing to the dedupe/refine hypotheses): the image-valley test separates same-nucleus from distinct-nucleus node pairs. valley = min smoothed intensity on the segment / min of the endpoint intensities; sigma z/y/x = 0.6/1.5/1.5 full-res voxels; start point = the brightest voxel within 2 um; distinct pairs have a median of 0.86 and 46% fall below 0.85, while same-blob pairs sit at about 1.0. It could veto duplicate insertions (divinsert, gap nodes, readmit) or drive merging of near-duplicate kept nodes 3-6 um apart that show no valley. refined_change: Drop the sandwich hole-fill as specified. If anything is kept, it is a narrowed DISTINCT-NUCLEUS fill that adds a sub-threshold peak q (from the >=0.90 peak cache / x138 lowdet dump) at frame t only if ALL of these hold. (a) Clearance >= 6.5 um from every kept node at t, instead of 4.5, so q cannot be the flank of an existing nucleus. (b) Image valley < 0.85 between q and its nearest kept node, from the smoothed raw frame with the parameters above; this is a GT-free check that q is a separate blob. (c) Chain support: peaks (cached or kept) within 4 um of q at t-1 AND t+1, with |q - midpoint| < 2 um, so the chain is a smooth trajectory. Chains of 3 or more such peaks are inserted as whole tracklets before the motion relink, so relink, gap1/gap2, the edge filter and stitch can attach them. Cap: +1.0% nodes per video, ranked by the minimum peak score along the chain. This is a variant of B35 step A / x138 gapfill (a new trigger, and the first one with an image-based duplicate guard), not new territory. Priority is below the coordinate head and duplicate suppression. For the 4-6 um holes (the real 'swap' mass) the lever is node position (x138 head, head retrained on 199 videos) and same-blob duplicate merging using the valley test, never node insertion.
refined_lab_test: STEP 0 (CPU; needs friend A's peaks90/<stem>.npz, or the x138 lowdet dump run on train; nothing local has sub-threshold peaks). For each cached peak not in the final graph, compute: clearance to kept nodes at t, the valley to the nearest kept node (raw zarr), and chain support at t-1/t+1. Report per embryo: (i) coverage = share of hole GT nodes with nearest node >7 um that have a triggered peak within 3 um, split by GT node; (ii) false-flank rate = share of triggered peaks within 3 um of a GT node whose nearest kept node is 4-6 um away, which must be <= 10% (otherwise the rule still creates duplicates); (iii) added nodes per video. GO only if coverage >= 20% in BOTH embryos at <= +1.0% nodes and the false-flank rate is <= 10%. As a control, also report what the ORIGINAL rule (clearance 4.5, sandwich 6 um) triggers: the prediction is that most of its fills at annotated cells land in the 4-6 um same-blob class. STEP 1: replay lab --patch holefill (insert the chains into the ILP solution, rerun relink via anatomy.relink_rerun, then gap/tail/ef/stitch). SELECTION (64 6bba) requires >= +0.003 with hole(>7 um)-FN down >= 15%, FP not up, and node ratio up by <= 1%. Then one standard CONFIRMATION run (>= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, >= 55% of videos gaining per embryo, CI > 0). Readouts: FN/FP split by nearest-node bin (<=4, 4-6, 6-7, >7 um), share of inserted nodes removed by the short-track filter, node ratio. Discount any local gain by at least 50% for public: the peaks come from a detector trained on these videos.
